scopeMarkdown:
Give `rayx` Linux guests it creates, keeps current and removes: a **Lima Ubuntu VM on macOS** (`rayx setup --lima`), next to the existing WSL distribution on Windows (`rayx setup --wsl`), and a **refresh** that keeps both guests and the host current when `rayx` updates.

## In scope

- **Ubuntu pin.** One Ubuntu version for every guest, `24.04`, in the built-in pins table. The WSL distribution name (`Ubuntu-24.04`) and the Lima template (`template:ubuntu-24.04`) derive from it. Lima's `template:ubuntu`/`ubuntu-lts` resolve to 26.04 in Lima 2.2.1, so the template is always named with the version.
- **Shared guest layer.** The WSL orchestration in `src/setup/wsl.rs` (install the matching Linux `rayx` with the release installer, clone the current checkout, run `rayx setup <flags>` inside) becomes guest-generic; WSL and Lima differ only in how a script runs inside (`wsl -d <name> --exec bash -lc` / `limactl shell --workdir / <name> -- bash -lc`) and how the guest is created.
- **`rayx setup --lima [--clone [<dir>]] [set flags]`** (macOS only): Lima through Homebrew, the VM `rayx` (vz, Ubuntu 24.04, defaults 6 CPUs, 12 GiB memory, 100 GiB disk, the macOS home mounted read-only, containerd off), the Linux `rayx` of the same version inside, the optional clone, and the same `rayx setup` inside.
- **VM sizing.** Defaults capped to what the Mac can spare, a `Customize? [y/N]` prompt on creation in a terminal, flags `--vm-cpus`, `--vm-memory`, `--vm-disk`, `--vm-home-writable` for unattended runs, and an offered stop, `limactl edit`, start when flags change an existing VM.
- **Records.** Every `rayx setup` run records its sets and project roots on the machine it ran on; `setup --wsl`/`--lima` record the guests they manage on the host.
- **`rayx doctor`** reports the rayx-managed guests (Lima VMs on macOS, WSL distributions on Windows): state, resources, home mount, Ubuntu version, current or retired, and the removal command for retired ones.
- **`rayx setup --update`** re-runs setup for the recorded sets on the host (no `apt-get upgrade` on a native Linux host) and refreshes every current guest: the matching Linux `rayx`, `apt-get update && apt-get upgrade`, and `rayx setup --update` inside.
- **`rayx self update`** offers that refresh with the new binary after it installs a newer release.
- **Side-by-side Ubuntu migration.** A guest older than the pin is replaced by a new guest from the pinned image (Lima: the old VM is renamed `rayx-<old version>`; WSL: `Ubuntu-<pin>` next to the old distribution), its clones and flags are restored, and the old guest is kept, retired, until the owner removes it.
- **Removal commands** `rayx lima remove <name>` and `rayx wsl remove <name>` for rayx-managed guests only, always confirmed.
- README and CLI help, and a manual verification on this Mac recorded in `docs/manual-verification.md`.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-14)

`--lima` as the flag; the VM is named `rayx`; defaults are capped on small Macs; one `Customize? [y/N]` prompt, then per-value prompts; offer stop, edit, start for an existing VM; `rayx doctor` reports the VM in v1; Ubuntu pinned to 24.04; side-by-side migration with commands to remove specific guests; guests run `apt-get upgrade`; the host is refreshed too, without `apt-get upgrade` on a native Linux host; `rayx setup --update` exists on its own and `rayx self update` calls it.

## Assumptions

- `--all` does not include `--lima` (a VM and a 620 MB image are not a host requirement); `--lima` is never implied.
- An existing VM is changed only by explicit `--vm-*` flags; a re-run without them asks nothing and executes nothing for the VM.
- Instances and distributions `rayx` did not create (for example the owner's `gpux` VM) are never started, stopped, edited, updated or removed.
- The guest's sudo: Lima configures passwordless sudo for the guest user; WSL asks in the console as today.

## Out of scope

- A `rayx lima status` command (doctor reports the VM), Lima on Linux hosts, QEMU or Rosetta options, GPU acceleration inside the VM (the guest uses lavapipe like WSL), snapshots, port forwards.
- Changing the RayX repository.
- In-place `do-release-upgrade`.
constraintsMarkdown:
- `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` rules hold: every external program through `host::Runner`; `rayx` never reads, stores or forwards a password or token and never relaunches itself elevated (`limactl` refuses root anyway); licenses only with `--yes` (Lima has none); `--check` executes, creates, records and downloads nothing.
- Existing setup rules hold inside and outside guests: probe before installing, a second run executes nothing, an outdated item is asked about (`--yes` updates without asking, no terminal and no `--yes` leaves it and exits 1), a first install is never asked about.
- WSL behaviour stays as it is except where a criterion here changes it (the pin-derived distribution name, the guest-neutral clones file, records, refresh, migration, removal).
- Nothing deletes a guest, a clone or build output without an explicit command and confirmation (or `--yes`); guests `rayx` did not create are never touched.
- GitHub's macOS runners cannot run VMs: automated tests drive `limactl`, `wsl` and `sysctl` through a recording runner with scripted responses; real-VM proof is manual.
- Tests are new feature groups in `tests/<feature>.rs`; while iterating run only the touched group. Conventional Commits with scopes, no co-author lines.

requirements.title: Ubuntu pin for guests
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: One Ubuntu version for every Linux guest, kept with the other built-in defaults.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
The built-in defaults table in `project::pins` holds the guest Ubuntu version `24.04` (source reported as built-in; a project cannot override it, since guests serve every project on the machine). No other module hard-codes an Ubuntu version: the WSL distribution name is `Ubuntu-<pin>` (`Ubuntu-24.04`) and the Lima template is `template:ubuntu-<pin>` (`template:ubuntu-24.04`), both computed from the pin. `rayx doctor` lists the pin with the other pins.

Verified by the new group `tests/guest_layer.rs` (pin value and source, both derived names, a changed pin in a test `Pins` value changing both names).

requirements.title: Shared guest layer
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: WSL and Lima share one implementation of what happens inside a Linux guest.

requirements.title: rayx setup --lima
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: From macOS, create and start the Lima VM `rayx` and set it up like a WSL distribution.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx setup` accepts `--lima` (help: set up the Lima VM `rayx` with Ubuntu <pin> on macOS and run the same setup inside it). `--lima` conflicts with `--wsl` and `--update`; `--clone [<dir>]` requires `--wsl` or `--lima`; `--vm-cpus <n>`, `--vm-memory <GiB>`, `--vm-disk <GiB>` (positive integers) and `--vm-home-writable` require `--lima`. On Windows or Linux, `setup --lima` exits 1 with `` `rayx setup --lima` creates a Lima VM on macOS `` and runs nothing; `setup --wsl` off Windows keeps its message. `--all` does not imply `--lima`.

Verified by the new group `tests/setup_lima.rs` (clap acceptance and rejections, the non-macOS error with no recorded command).

The VM is created only when `limactl list --json` has no instance `rayx` (output is one JSON object per line; memory and disk are bytes):

`limactl create --tty=false --name=rayx --vm-type=vz --cpus=<n> --memory=<GiB> --disk=<GiB> --mount-only=<home>[:w] --containerd=none template:ubuntu-<pin>`, then `limactl start --tty=false rayx`, which waits until the VM is ready. `<home>` is the macOS home; `:w` only with a writable choice.

An existing stopped `rayx` is started; a running one is left alone. A second `setup --lima` without `--vm-*` flags runs no `limactl` command that changes anything (only `list`, version and probes). `--check` prints every command that would run, including the create line, and runs only read-only queries. Instances with other names are never started, stopped or edited.

Verified by `tests/setup_lima.rs` (absent, stopped and running instance; exact create arguments; read-only home default; `--check` records only queries; another instance untouched).

Through the guest layer, `setup --lima` then installs the Linux `rayx` of the same version in the VM (release installer, or `RAYX_LIMA_BINARY`), clones the current checkout with `--clone [<dir>]` and runs `rayx setup <set flags, --check, --yes>` inside, in the clone when one was made.

The clone source is the host checkout path, which the VM mounts at the same path; a checkout outside the macOS home exits 1 with `--clone needs a checkout under <home>, which the VM mounts`. Default target `~/<checkout name>` in the guest home.

Verified by `tests/setup_lima.rs` (the script commands through `limactl shell --workdir / rayx -- bash -lc`, inner flags, the clone script, the outside-home refusal).

Sizing defaults are 6 CPUs, 12 GiB memory, 100 GiB disk and the home read-only. The host is read with `sysctl -n hw.ncpu hw.memsize` and `df -k` on the Lima home volume:

- CPU cap: `max(1, ncpu - 2)`; memory cap: `max(2, floor(total GiB / 2))`. A default above its cap is lowered to the cap and a note names the host (`this Mac has 16 GiB memory: the VM gets 8 GiB`).
- Explicit values (flags or prompts) above the cap, CPUs below 1, memory below 2 GiB or disk below 30 GiB are refused with the allowed range: a flag exits 1 before any `limactl` command; a prompt asks again.
- Fewer than 10 GiB free on the Lima home volume exits 1; free space below the chosen disk size prints a note (the disk image is sparse).
- When running Lima VMs (any name) plus the new VM would exceed three quarters of the host memory, a warning names them.

Verified by the new group `tests/setup_lima_sizing.rs` with hosts of 8, 16 and 24 GiB and 8 and 10 cores.

When the VM is about to be created, in a terminal and without `--yes`, `rayx` prints the effective settings (defaults after caps, then flags) and asks once: `Create Lima VM rayx: <n> CPUs, <m> GiB memory, <d> GiB disk, home mounted read-only. Customize? [y/N]`. `y` asks for CPUs, memory and disk (Enter keeps the shown value, invalid input asks again with the range) and `Mount the home writable? [y/N]`. Without a terminal, or with `--yes`, nothing is asked and the effective settings are used. Prompts go through an injectable prompter so tests script the answers.

Verified by `tests/setup_lima_sizing.rs` (no, yes with each value changed, invalid then valid input, `--yes`, no terminal).

`--vm-*` flags on an existing `rayx` that differ from it (CPUs, memory, disk from `limactl list --json`; home writability from its `lima.yaml` mounts) are an update: listed (`4 -> 6 CPUs`), asked about per the outdated rule (`--yes` applies without asking; no terminal and no `--yes` reports and exits 1), and applied as `limactl stop rayx` (only when running), `limactl edit --tty=false rayx <changed flags>` (`--mount-only=<home>[:w]` for the home), `limactl start --tty=false rayx`. A smaller disk is refused (Lima cannot shrink a disk) and nothing runs. Flags equal to the VM change nothing.

Verified by the new group `tests/setup_lima_edit.rs`.

requirements.title: Setup and guest records
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: What `rayx setup` did is recorded, so a later refresh, doctor and removal know it.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
A successful `rayx setup --wsl` or `--lima` (not `--check`) records the guest on the host in `<config>/rayx/guests.json` (`<config>`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config` on Unix, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows): a versioned document with, per guest, `kind` (`wsl`/`lima`), `name`, `ubuntu` (the guest's `VERSION_ID`), the set flags it was set up with (union over runs), its clones (`source`, `branch`, `target`), for Lima the settings it was created with, and `retired` (false). A rerun updates the entry instead of adding one. A missing or unreadable file is an empty record; an unparsable one is reported and left untouched. The record holds no secrets.

Verified by the new group `tests/guest_records.rs`.

A successful `rayx setup` run that installs or checks a plan (not `--check`, not `--wsl`/`--lima` on the outer side) records on the machine it ran on, in `<config>/rayx/setup.json`, the union of the sets it ran and the project workspace root it ran in (when there was one). A setup inside a guest records in the guest. `--check` records nothing.

Verified by the new group `tests/setup_update.rs`.

requirements.title: Doctor reports guests
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: `rayx doctor` shows the rayx-managed guests of this host.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
On macOS `rayx doctor` reports Lima (`limactl` version or missing with `rayx setup --lima`) and every Lima guest in `guests.json` joined with `limactl list --json`: name, status (running, stopped, missing), CPUs, memory, disk, home read-only or writable, Ubuntu version, current or retired, and for a retired or missing guest the command that removes it (`rayx lima remove <name>`). On Windows the recorded WSL guests are reported the same way (`rayx wsl remove <name>`). `--json` adds a `guests` array with the same fields. Doctor never starts a VM, and its exit code stays 0 whenever the host could be inspected.

Verified by `tests/guest_records.rs` (text and JSON for running, stopped, retired and missing guests; Lima missing).

requirements.title: rayx setup --update
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Bring the host and every current guest up to the running `rayx` and its pins.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx setup --update [--yes] [--check]` (conflicts with set flags, `--wsl`, `--lima`, `--clone`, `--vm-*`) re-runs the setup plan for the recorded sets once per recorded project root that still exists (in that root, so the project's pins apply; a vanished root is reported and dropped from the record), or once without a project when none is recorded. Outdated items follow the outdated rule. On a native Linux host it runs no `apt-get upgrade` (missing packages are still installed). With nothing recorded it prints `nothing recorded: run \`rayx setup\` first` and exits 0.

Verified by `tests/setup_update.rs` (two project roots with different pins, a vanished root, no record, no `apt-get upgrade` on Linux).

requirements.title: Self update refreshes
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A `rayx` update is followed by the refresh it makes possible.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx self update` gains `--yes`. After it installed a newer release, and only when `setup.json` or `guests.json` exists: in a terminal without `--yes` it asks `Refresh this machine's setup and guests with rayx <new>? [y/N]`; yes, or `--yes`, runs the executable at the path `rayx` was started from (captured before the install, so Windows' renamed old binary is never used) as `setup --update [--yes]` with inherited stdio, and its exit code becomes the command's. No, or no terminal and no `--yes`, prints `run \`rayx setup --update\` to refresh the setup and guests` and exits 0. `--check`, an up-to-date `rayx` and a failed install never refresh.

Verified by the new group `tests/self_update_refresh.rs` with the fake update backend.

requirements.title: Side-by-side Ubuntu migration
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: When the pin moves to a newer Ubuntu, a guest is replaced by a new one next to it, never upgraded in place.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`setup --update`, `setup --wsl` and `setup --lima` read the current guest's `VERSION_ID`. Below the pin, the guest is outdated: `rayx` lists the clones in it that hold uncommitted changes or commits on no remote (`git status --porcelain`, `git log --branches --not --remotes`), says the old guest is kept, and asks `Create <new guest> with Ubuntu <pin> next to <old guest>? [y/N]` per the outdated rule. Declined or unanswerable: nothing changes and the guest is reported outdated (exit 1). A guest newer than the pin is reported and left alone. No `do-release-upgrade` ever runs.

Verified by the new group `tests/guest_migration.rs`.

Lima migration: `limactl stop rayx`, `limactl rename rayx rayx-<old version>` (the record is updated right away: renamed and retired), then the new `rayx` is created from `template:ubuntu-<pin>` with the old VM's CPUs, memory, disk and home mount (no customize prompt), started, given the Linux `rayx`, the recorded clones (re-cloned from their host sources) and `rayx setup <recorded flags>` per clone, and recorded as current. A rerun after an interruption resumes from the record (a renamed old VM is not renamed again). Completion prints `rayx lima remove rayx-<old version>`.

Verified by `tests/guest_migration.rs` (command sequence, record after each step, resume after a failed create).

WSL migration: `wsl --install -d Ubuntu-<pin>` next to the old distribution (which stays registered and is recorded as retired once the new one is set up); the new distribution's first-user stop works as today and a rerun continues; then the Linux `rayx`, the recorded clones from their Windows sources and `rayx setup <recorded flags>` per clone. Completion prints `rayx wsl remove <old name>`.

Verified by `tests/guest_migration.rs`.

requirements.title: Guest removal
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Commands that remove one specific rayx-managed guest.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`rayx lima remove <name> [--yes]` (macOS) runs `limactl delete --force <name>`; `rayx wsl remove <name> [--yes]` (Windows) runs `wsl --unregister <name>`. Both drop the guest from `guests.json` after the command succeeded and report what was removed. Removing the current guest says that `rayx setup --lima`/`--wsl` creates it again.

Verified by the new group `tests/guest_remove.rs`.

Removal is refused (exit 1, nothing runs) for a name not in `guests.json` (`<name> was not created by rayx; remove it with limactl delete / wsl --unregister yourself`) and on the wrong OS. Before removing, `rayx` lists clones in the guest with uncommitted or unpushed work (when the guest can be inspected without starting it) and asks `Remove <name> and everything in it? [y/N]`; without a terminal and without `--yes` it refuses and exits 1. `--yes` removes without asking.

Verified by `tests/guest_remove.rs` (unrecorded name, the owner's `gpux` shape untouched, declined, no terminal, `--yes`).

requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The README and CLI help describe the new commands.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`README.md` documents `setup --lima` (what it creates, defaults and caps, the customize prompt, `--vm-*` flags, read-only home and why `--clone` is how a checkout is built in the VM, existing-VM changes), the records, `setup --update`, the refresh after `self update`, side-by-side migration, `rayx lima remove` and `rayx wsl remove`, and doctor's guest report. Every new flag and subcommand has help text.

Verified by the new group `tests/readme_guests.rs` (README sections and `--help` output of `setup`, `self update`, `lima remove`, `wsl remove`).

requirements.title: Real hosts
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The flows work against real Lima and WSL, recorded in `docs/manual-verification.md`.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: On this Mac (Apple silicon, Lima 2.2.1, the owner's `gpux` VM running and untouched): `rayx setup --lima --vm-cpus 2 --vm-memory 4 --web --clone` from a checkout under the home creates `rayx` (vz, Ubuntu 24.04, home read-only: a write under the mounted home fails inside), installs the Linux `rayx` from `RAYX_LIMA_BINARY`, clones, and the inner setup finishes; a second run prints nothing to do for the VM; the customize prompt is exercised once interactively; `rayx doctor` shows the VM; `--vm-cpus 3` on the existing VM goes through stop, edit, start. Recorded with date and results.

On this Mac with local builds: `rayx setup --update` refreshes the host and `rayx` (apt upgrade, inner `setup --update`); a local build whose pin is temporarily `26.04` (not committed) migrates side by side (`rayx-24.04` retired and kept, new `rayx` on 26.04 with the clone restored); `rayx lima remove rayx-24.04` and finally `rayx lima remove rayx` remove both after confirmation while `gpux` keeps running. Recorded with date and results.

Owner-run on the Windows PC: `rayx setup --wsl --web --clone` still works with the guest layer, `guests.json` lists `Ubuntu-24.04`, `rayx setup --update` refreshes it (apt upgrade, inner update), and `rayx doctor` reports it. Recorded with date and results.

Owner-run after the first release that contains this epic: `rayx self update` from the previous release on the Mac (and on Windows) installs it and offers the refresh, which updates the guest. Recorded with date, versions and results.
